title: Allow text to be copied
line: You can now copy the playing track's title and artist from the Media Player widget's context menu, or with Ctrl+C in its popup.
explanation: The Media Player widget shows the track title and artist as plain labels and offers no way to copy them, so people listening to web radio had to type the song out by hand to note it down. The change adds a "Copy Title and Artist" item ("Copy Title" when there is no artist) to the widget's context menu, shown only while there is a track, and makes Ctrl+C in the open popup do the same. Both copy "Title – Artist" to the clipboard.

commits.message:
applets/mediacontroller: allow copying the title and artist

There was no way to copy the title and artist of the playing track, so
people had to type them out by hand. Add a "Copy Title and Artist" item
to the context menu, and copy the same text with Ctrl+C in the popup.

BUG: 409988

media.caption: Right-clicking the Media Player icon offers only playback controls
The context menu now has "Copy Title and Artist"
After using it (and Ctrl+C in the popup), the clipboard holds "Strobe – deadmau5"
A track without an artist offers "Copy Title" and copies just the title

reviews.text: Clean, minimal implementation that adds a "Copy Title and Artist" (or "Copy Title" when there is no artist) contextual action and Ctrl+C (StandardKey.Copy) support in the Media Player popup. It uses proper KDE i18n contexts and a translatable format string, hides the action and separator cleanly when no track is playing, and directly addresses the reporter's workflow without introducing accidental text selection.

Gives the reporter what they asked for (right-click, then copy title and artist) and implements Oliver's Ctrl+C suggestion from c3 too. It follows the existing contextualActions pattern and avoids the accidental-selection worry with selectable labels. The code is small and correct: the action is shown only when there is a track, the label switches to 'Copy Title' with no artist, the format string is translatable with a context, and it uses KQuickControlsAddons.Clipboard, which plasma-workspace already uses. The evidence covers the menu, clipboard contents, the popup shortcut and the no-artist case.
